findings.reason: the plan's §3 measure is "dispatch and observe stop writing session fields onto roster members", and a member-named entry point kept for compatibility leaves the retired contract reachable by name; the honest change is to delete it and call `capture_run_session` directly.
findings.text: `_capture_member_session(record)` is defined as `return capture_run_session(record)` with the docstring "Compatibility entry point for promotion; capture writes only the run", so it is a bare alias over `capture_run_session` (reckon/crew/runs.py:79) with no added behaviour; it is the surviving name of the retired roster-capture contract and every caller is a direct one (reckon/crew/promotion.py:5365, 8169, 8679; reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11091)

findings.reason: the plan's §2/§9 falsifier names the `blocking_limit` / `Prompt is too long` endings as the withheld-session condition, so the reading is the plan's own contract; the file to extend is `reckon/crew/context_budget.py`, which already owns the context-refusal and compact_boundary vocabulary, and the shared reader is `reckon/_backends.py:3620`.
findings.text: `_session_too_large_to_continue` opens and re-decodes a run's stream itself (dispatch.py:11272) for the same events two owners already decode: `context_budget.py:25-26` owns the literals `"Prompt is too long"` and `"system/compact_boundary"` (dispatch.py:11294,11291) and `recovery._admission_refusal` owns `terminal_reason == "blocking_limit"` (dispatch.py:11298 vs recovery.py:4950); it also bypasses the shared decoded-stream cache `_backends.cached_stream_events` (reckon/_backends.py:3620) that recovery.py:4932 uses, so the file is parsed a second time per decision

findings.reason: §9 names "a redispatched-then-resumed run launches with the new harness's own session" as the section's done-when, which is exactly the lane_change path; the selection decision should ask `_current_harness_session` rather than re-deriving harness ownership from a narrower field set, or the two must be pinned together by a test the plan already lists.
findings.text: the "which harness owns this session" rule is implemented twice in the same module: `_task_session_resolution` compares `owner != harness` from `session_harness`/`dialect` (dispatch.py:11441-11453), and `_current_harness_session` (dispatch.py:11558-11599) implements the same rule plus the `lane_change` boundary (`changed_harness`) and the fresh-observation fallback; the incomplete copy at 11450 will drift from the more complete owner from the more complete owner as lane-change handling evolves

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; the task-keyed selection is one call, `_task_session_resolution` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11392), which hides the run-record join, the withhold-verdict and the held-session check behind a single return, and the resume side keeps its reader in the module that already owns session reading, `resolve_session` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:464).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `_session_too_large_to_continue` re-parsing a run's stream duplicates the event vocabulary and the cached stream reader that other modules already own.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan ran a reuse map before proposing machinery (§1, 34 site rows, all five falsifier sites present) and the landed decision cites the mechanism it replaced, `_member_session_resolution`, and its successor `_task_session_resolution` at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11392.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `_capture_member_session` is a compatibility alias that forwards to `capture_run_session` and adds nothing.
